title: Soldier, to the Contest Pressing
description: Soldier, to the Contest Pressing in Tonic Solfa to GALILEE (JUDE), doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 992 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Soldier of the Cross”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to GALILEE (JUDE); any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sol-dier, to the con-test press-ing, On-ward, let thy watch-word be; God up-on thee pours his bless-ing; What though man de-ri-deth thee!

lines: God upon thee pours his blessing;
Onward in the path of right!
God, for all thy wants providing,
And thy feet with justice shod:
Wield thy sword, the word of God.
Faith thy mighty shield shall be;
In the path the martyrs trod:
God to thee his strength is lending;
Onward, in the strength of God.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to GALILEE (JUDE) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
